title: RailGrid Capacity Solutions
text:
RailGrid Capacity Solutions

notes:
Deal background: RailGrid is a fleet-management SaaS used by Class I rail operators in NA. They evaluated hosted APIs but require dedicated capacity and strict residency. Procurement stage; heavy focus on SLA/credits and guaranteed throughput for peak windows.

Key quote from CTO on 2026-02-10 call: "If trains are delayed because inference spikes, operators lose millions — SLA has to be ironclad."

SLA negotiation summary (current ask):
- Target uptime: 99.95% monthly (RailGrid wants 99.99% on core routing endpoints if possible).
- Credit schedule proposed by Redwood (counter-proposal in progress): tiered credits: <99.95% -> 10% monthly credit; <99.9% -> 25%; <99.5% -> 50%; catastrophic (<95%) -> termination right + pro-rated refund. Legal pushing to formalize measurement window and aggregation rules.
- Maintenance windows: preference = 03:00-05:00 UTC monthly, 48h scheduled notice. RailGrid requires clause for no major upgrades during critical seasonal run (Nov 01 - Mar 31) except emergency patches with 4h notice and automatic fallback to previous model variant.
- Support & response: they insist on 24/7 escalation path. Proposed SRT: P1 (service down/critical impact) = 30 min acknowledge / 1h mitigation commitment; P2 (degraded perf) = 4h acknowledge / 12h mitigation plan; P3 (minor) = next-business-day. SLA to include on-call engineer contact and monthly on-call postmortem for P1 incidents.

Technical & capacity planning notes:
- Baseline reserved: 12x A100-equivalent GPUs (initial), with option to scale to 20 for seasonal peak.
- Baseline concurrency target: 120 concurrent sessions (chat) with average session QPS ~1.2; expected burst concurrency up to 400 for 10-15 minute windows during incident reroutes.
- Throughput guarantees: 150K tokens/min sustained per deployment for reranking pipelines; 95% of requests p95 latency target <= 220ms for small instruction models (<=2k tokens); p99 <= 700ms when KV cache used.
- Latency SLOs asked by customer: p50 < 60ms (local-cache hits), p95 < 220ms, p99 < 700ms for production routing endpoint. Redwood proposed p95 < 300ms as realistic for first 3 months while tuning batching/quantization.
- Fallback policy: must support automatic fallback to smaller quantized model within 250ms if primary model exceeds latency SLO for >30s. Customer wants explicit routing priority: dedicated -> burst -> hosted-fallback.

POC milestones so far:
- 2026-01-18: Architecture review (network/topology) — done.
- 2026-01-26: Security questionnaire (SOC2, KMS integration) — completed; awaiting KMS key rotation procedure confirmation.
- 2026-02-05: Load test #1 (synthetic traces) — measured p95 ~320ms at target concurrency; Redwood suggested batching changes.
- 2026-02-24: Load test #2 (with KV cache + dynamic batching) — p95 improved to ~210ms; RailGrid requested written throughput guarantees.
- 2026-02-28: SLA draft v2 sent to RailGrid legal.

Procurement/legal asks outstanding:
- Precise SLA measurement and exclusion clauses for scheduled maintenance vs unplanned outages.
- Definitive credit calculation example (month with one 45-minute partial outage -> what credit).
- Escrow of model weights clause for disaster recovery (RailGrid wants express language).

Commercial notes:
- ACV target: $300k-$1M ARR; preference for 12–24 month reserved commit with quarterly true-ups.
- Pricing sensitivity: willing to trade some credits for price — legal asked for a tiered option: higher uptime for +10% fee.

Sales motion / internal ask: need legal to provide one clean SLA option for customer sign-off (A & B: A=99.99% @ +10% cost; B=99.95% standard). Request RD to prepare final MSA redline and run through Escalation review on 2026-03-08.

Short-term next steps (client-facing):
- Send final credit schedule matrix and two SLA options by 2026-03-07.
- Confirm exact reserved GPU spec (A100 vs H100) and pricing delta.
- Align maintenance windows with RailGrid ops calendar and produce explicit blackout dates for Q4.

Internal notes: procurement timeline aggressive — procurement expects decision by 2026-04. If legal stalls, drop to backup plan: propose 6-month pilot with higher observability clauses instead of full commit.
